questions.explain: The chapter's loop has four stages — detect, classify, act, verify — enforced by invariants: no action without classification, no incident closed without verification, and repeated failures escalate rather than loop forever.
options: Detect, alert, page, post-mortem
Observe, decide, act
Detect, classify, act, verify
Snapshot, analyze, execute, log
questions.q: What are the four stages of the chapter's remediation loop, and what invariant applies to each?

questions.explain: In the RemediationLoop, when attempts are exhausted or verification fails after 5 checks, the state moves to ESCALATED/FAILED and the escalation hook fires — never looping silently forever.
options: Retry the same action indefinitely until it succeeds
Double the aggressiveness of the playbook each time
Silently mark the incident resolved after 3 attempts
Route to ESCALATED state and fire the escalation hook, capping retries with exponential backoff
questions.q: In the remediation loop implementation, what happens when action attempts are exhausted or verification fails repeatedly?

questions.explain: The kill policy must check: is the session a protected known scheduled job, is blocking duration below tolerance (e.g. 60s OLTP / 300s batch), and is the application name on a protected list — only then does it terminate.
options: Verify the session is not a protected scheduled job, blocking duration exceeds tolerance (60s OLTP / 300s batch), and the application name is not on a protected list
Check that the session has been idle for at least 30 minutes
Confirm the session belongs to the sa login
Verify the blocking chain depth is greater than 10
questions.q: Before killing a root blocker session, what three conditions must the chapter's kill decision policy evaluate?

questions.explain: Automatic failover only fires when the secondary is SYNCHRONIZED; a SYNCHRONIZING secondary will not be promoted automatically. Quorum must be retained, and flexible failover policy Level 3 is a common production starting point.
options: Any secondary, regardless of synchronization state
Only replicas with log send queues under 10 MB
Only a secondary in SYNCHRONIZED state; a SYNCHRONIZING secondary will not be promoted automatically
Only manual failover is ever supported
questions.q: What synchronization requirement must a secondary meet before an availability group automatic failover fires?

questions.explain: The chapter's graduated response: 10-30% fragmentation → REORGANIZE; >30% or ghost accumulation → REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON) in the maintenance window; high forwarded records on a heap → clustered index creation or table rebuild.
options: REBUILD immediately for any fragmentation above 5%
REORGANIZE for 10-30%, REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON) above 30% or when ghost records accumulate, and clustered index creation/rebuild for high forwarded-record heaps
Disable the index and wait 72 hours
Shrink the database files
questions.q: What is the chapter's graduated space-management response for index fragmentation and ghost/forwarded records?
